notes.Nikola Jokic: He has played 36 and 37 minutes in his last two games and posted 59.25 DraftKings points Monday with 26 points, nine rebounds, eight assists and four steals. Toronto is without Kawhi Leonard, and this game carries the slate's highest total at 230.5 points.
notes.Jayson Tatum: He is listed as questionable for Wednesday against Milwaukee for rest, so his status is worth checking before lock. He has played 32 to 35 minutes in each of his last three games with 26, 32 and 19 points, and the 11.5-point spread adds blowout risk if he plays.
notes.Shai Gilgeous-Alexander: He scored 43 points with eight assists in 39 minutes Monday against Cleveland, his heaviest workload of the season. Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace are all out again for the rematch, while Alex Caruso is off the report and takes back some ball handling.
notes.Scottie Barnes: With Kawhi Leonard out again, he has played 36 to 39 minutes in each of his last three games and had 22 points, 15 rebounds and eight assists Monday. Jakob Poeltl is questionable with shoulder bursitis, and Toronto has used Barnes at center at times.
notes.Alperen Sengun: He returned from a back injury Monday with 26 points, seven rebounds and 10 assists in 38 minutes. Steven Adams is out and Clint Capela is questionable, which keeps the center minutes on Sengun, and Minnesota is without Anthony Edwards.
notes.Meleek Thomas: He started Monday with Jaylon Tyson and Peyton Watson out and scored 17 points in 26 minutes. Both are out again Wednesday at Oklahoma City, so the starting spot should stay his.
notes.Quenton Jackson: Tyrese Haliburton and T.J. McConnell are out again, and he started Monday for 20 points, seven rebounds and four steals in 35 minutes. Indiana rested several regulars that night, so his minutes shrink if those regulars return.
notes.Jerami Grant: He has played 23 to 27 minutes off the bench in each of his last three games and scored 14 and 11 in the last two. Scotty Pippen Jr. is out again, which keeps Grant's bench role steady.
notes.Deandre Ayton: He started at center Monday with Alex Sarr out and played 24 minutes, but managed only four points and six rebounds. Sarr is questionable with knee soreness, so Ayton's role depends on that call, and the game has a 233.5-point total.
notes.Kingston Flemings: He is back from a one-game suspension after 12 points, six assists and four steals in 25 minutes off the bench Saturday. Jalen Johnson is questionable with an ankle sprain, which would open more minutes for Atlanta's guards and wings.
notes.Jay Huff: He has started every game since Oct. 26 with Ivica Zubac out and had 22 points, eight rebounds and two blocks in 40 minutes Monday, when Indiana rested its regulars. Zubac is questionable Wednesday, and Huff played only 17 and 19 minutes in the two games before Monday.
notes.Bilal Coulibaly: He has come off the bench since AJ Dybantsa joined the starting lineup, but played 33 minutes Monday. Alex Sarr is questionable, which could open more frontcourt minutes in a game with a 233.5-point total.
notes.Aaron Nesmith: He is not on Indiana's injury report after sitting Monday, when the Pacers rested regulars. He started and played 30 minutes Sunday, and Tyrese Haliburton, T.J. McConnell and Ben Sheppard are all out again.
notes.Kon Knueppel: He is listed as probable at Brooklyn, which would be his first game back from a hamstring strain. Expect his minutes to be managed in the return.
notes.Alex Caruso: He is off the injury report for Wednesday against Cleveland. His return takes minutes from Oklahoma City's bench guards and wings with Cason Wallace and Jalen Williams out.
